#719. English female coach Kaminski reaping rewards in Norway

Laura Kaminski guided Crystal Palace to the WSL 2 title in 2024

When English manager Laura Kaminski was approached to become the head coach of Norwegian club SK Brann in January, she could not turn it down.

She jumped at the opportunity to move abroad and develop her coaching skills and is even competing for a place in the Europa Cup quarter-finals next Wednesday.

It was a decision that paid off as 10 months later, she is celebrating a Norwegian league and cup double after a dream debut season.

"My time in the city [of Bergen] has been brilliant," the 38-year-old told BBC Sport.

"I can't go to the supermarket at the minute because so many people are stopping me to wish me congratulations, which is so nice.

"I'm over the moon and it was nice to get the title done before the last game so we can relax. I thought it was going to go right to the wire.

"It's been a competitive year. I've enjoyed every minute. We had a great night with all our fans, who were waiting for us to return from Oslo."

Find interviews and extra content on the BBC Women's Football Weekly feed

Kaminski described it as a "hectic" year as she moved from London to Norway and away from her family to take on the Brann job.

The Englishwoman had spent over a year at Crystal Palace, where she led them to promotion to the Women's Super League in 2024.

She was sacked in February 2025 after a tough WSL season as Palace struggled to compete with better financially-backed clubs.

However, she is regarded as one of the country's brightest female managers and has added to her CV with her experiences in Norway.

"I've learned a lot. It's been chaotic - I counted that I have taken 65 flights in 11 months - so it's been exhausting, but what an experience!" added Kaminski.

"To go all the way up to the Arctic Circle and play away [games] in freezing cold conditions with horizontal snow, to beautiful days in Bergen.

"Palace was totally different to Brann. I'm at a club that expects to win the Toppserien [the Norwegian top-flight] as they believe they have invested the most.

"That's been a real challenge. The WSL is dominated by the favourites in the pack so it wasn't always the expectation to get three points against big teams [at Palace]."

Kaminski admits being away from loved ones is "hard" and she has had to be prepared to "make sacrifices" but Brann's trophy success makes it worth it.

She has also picked up new ideas for her coaching philosophy having experienced the high-risk, attack-minded football in Norway.

"Norwegian teams are almost guaranteed to concede every game because they play such attacking football with no fear, and a relentlessness to press," she added.

"That is a bit different to what I was used to. When I watched the tactical displays when I first came in, I was a little bit alarmed at what people were doing.

"But when you play against their sides, and against that [pressing], it is really difficult. It's given me a lot of fuel for the future.

"There are some really fit, fast and athletic players here. It's not a surprise that big, big clubs are coming in for them."

Laura Kaminski spent a year and a half at Crystal Palace

After a season in Norway, Kaminski believes she is a better coach.

She had spent over 15 years as an assistant manager at various clubs in the WSL 2 and WSL and a coaching role with England's under-19s before joining Palace.

But having added European experience to her CV, Kaminski hopes it will open the door to more opportunities in the future.

"I'd like to think I've got a well-rounded skillset to be able to manage at the top level. Right now, my focus is on Brann and a new chapter," said Kaminski.

"There's only two levels in England that are professional. I definitely wanted to get European exposure, which I was never going to get in England.

"At the time, I was in discussions with a few clubs but it was things that I'd done before, or the project wasn't matching.

"I knew that when I came to Brann, I was going to coach top-level players. I wanted to be at the top of the competition and I was desperate to win a trophy."

Kaminski has urged other female coaches in England to go abroad and gain experience as she believes opportunities are too few in the WSL.

A study from UK Coaching in October showed there has been a 6% decline in the overall number of female coaches in recent years.

There are currently three English female coaches in the WSL - Jo Potter at Crystal Palace, Amy Merricks at Birmingham City and Karen Hills at Charlton Athletic - and they all came up with promoted clubs this summer.

But Kaminski says she is "concerned" about where they might go next and hopes more opportunities in English men's football will open up soon.

"I ended up leaving the country to go and get what I thought I deserved and had earned the right to work in, in terms of the level," said Kaminski.

"There's more than one female out there that's capable [of working in men's football]. I don't think it's out of reach. I would always, certainly, be open to it.

"At the moment, for me, there's not enough consideration even for that opportunity to be given to female managers who are more than capable.

"I think the foundations are there for females to take the plunge but is the world of football ready? I'm unsure."

#718. IIHF ordered to allow Russia back into world championships

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has ruled that Russian teams must be allowed to take part in international ice hockey tournaments. The IIHF had banned Russia following the country's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

In a statement published on Friday, the Court of Arbitration for Sport(CAS) said it had overturned International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) decisions, which exclude Russia from events during the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships.

In the statement, the CAS cited a lack of sufficient evidence to support security concerns cited by the IIHF in its decisions to exclude Russian teams from competition.

Specifically, it ordered the IIHF to allow Russia to participate in five upcoming tournaments, including the Men's Ice Hockey World Championship in Germany next May and the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship scheduled for November 2027 in Canada.

The first tournament affected by the ruling is the Men's World Junior Championship, which opens in Edmonton on December 26. The Women's World Championship being hosted by Denmark starting next Friday, November 6, is not mentioned in the statement.

Russian Sports Minister Mikhail Degtyaryov hailed the CAS ruling, writing on the Telegram social media app that CAS had "recognized the demands of the Russian Hockey Federation on key points as justified."

The IIHF expressed disappointment with the ruling , saying it "maintains that its decisions were necessary to protect the safety and security of all participants and safeguard the integrity of its competitions."

"While the IIHF respects the authority of CAS and will act in accordance with its ruling, the outcome does not remove the concerns that informed its assessments."

Germany's ice hockey association, the DEB, also expressed disappointment at the decision.

"Our position is unchanged: We reject the return of Russian national teams to international ice hockey tournaments," said DEB chairman Frank Lutz, who added that the ruling had fundamentally changed things for Germany as hosts of the 2027 Men's World Championship.

"Allowing Russia to participate entails significant security-related, political, and economic consequences for us as hosts. We are now evaluating the ruling together with the IIHF and will provide information regarding the next steps."

In its statement, the IIHF also pointed to "significant practical implications for competitions already at an advanced stage of preparation," which includes the men's tournament to be hosted by Düsseldorf, Mannheim and Gelsenkirchen and for which the groups have already been drawn.

Among the teams slated to participate in the tournament are Ukraine, who are set to make their return to ice hockey's international top flight after winning promotion at this year's Division 1 tournament in Poland. Ukraine had spent two decades in international ice hockey's second tier since being relegated in 2007.

Unsurprisingly, the Ukranian federation (FHU) has also condemned the CAS decision.

"The Ice Hockey Federation of Ukraine respects the authority and status of the CAS. At the same time, we express our deep indignation at this decision, made amidst a full-scale war," it said in a statement.

"The threats that served as the basis for the suspension of Russian teams in 2022 have not disappeared; on the contrary, they have only intensified."

The IIHF has barred Russian teams from its tournaments since shortly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. This meant Russia also missed this year's prestigious Olympic hockey tournaments in Milan earlier this year.

Russia and its predecessor, the Soviet Union, are one of the most successful ice hockey-playing nations, having won 27 men's World Championships, second only to Canada (28).

Friday's ruling comes with the IIHF having just elected a new president – Germany's Franz Reindl took over from Luc Tardif of France earlier this month.

#717. Another 'miracle' in Istanbul - but this one hurt Liverpool

Liverpool suffer first Champions League loss to Fenerbahce

When it comes to comebacks, Liverpool and Istanbul have plenty of history - but this time Andoni Iraola's side made the wrong kind.

Having hit the front for a second time against Fenerbahce, when Alexander Isak nodded in after 69 minutes, Liverpool were seemingly on their way to a thoroughly impressive away win.

But Iraola's players then capitulated amid a febrile atmosphere, as spirited hosts led by interim boss Dirk Kuyt - a Liverpool hero of years gone by - pulled off a shock Champions League comeback victory.

By losing 3-2 at the Sukru Saracoglu stadium, Iraola's visitors created that unwanted slice of history: this was the latest Liverpool have ever gone ahead in a major European game and then been beaten.

Iraola described the goals they conceded as "cheap" and "messy".

After Liverpool let three points slip from their grasp, Kuyt spoke of how he had encouraged Fenerbahce's players to embrace the never-say-die mindset that allowed the Reds to achieve so many great feats in Europe in the past.

He joined Liverpool in 2006, a year after the team's famous 'Miracle of Istanbul' comeback in the Champions League final, and spent six years at Anfield.

"We told each other to stick together and be united. That's something I learned from Liverpool, who we played against," Kuyt said. "We made a miracle tonight - not many expected us to win."

He and Fenerbahce will remember this one for a long time. Liverpool will want to quickly forget it.

After winning five games in a row, Iraola's side have gone on to lose twice in four days. Arsenal on Sunday, and now this.

On their overnight flight back from Istanbul, there will be plenty of disappointment at the way in which Liverpool failed to see this game out.

"It's frustration because it's a difficult place to come and play," said Iraola. "We were, during most part of the game, thinking we can win this one. But obviously it hasn't happened."

All three of Fenerbahce's goals came from set-pieces.

Former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood benefited from a slice of luck when his free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet in the first half for Fenerbahce's first equaliser, and Liverpool only had themselves to blame when Cody Gakpo's header took the ball past Alisson and gave Birmingham-born Archie Brown a tap in to make it 2-2.

Six minutes later, Liverpool made a mess of Brown's looping ball in the box and Vedat Muriqi beat three players in red and headed past Alisson.

"They are cheap goals. They are messy goals," said Iraola.

"It's a free-kick. It's quite far also and it's through the wall.

"Mistakes can cost you. For the last goal, it's a long throw and the first phase is controlled but after a very long ball, Muriqi wins it.

"The second goal, Cody [Gakpo] is the one touching the ball just in front of Ali [Alisson].

"In the stadium it was almost impossible to communicate because it was so noisy. It was even difficult for me to give any kind of instruction. I suppose the communication between Ali and Cody was difficult."

Liverpool lost 3-2 having twice been ahead against Fenerbahce

Kuyt's Fenerbahce fight back to beat Liverpool

Why Iraola's Liverpool are still a work in progress

After showing signs of genuine progress in recent weeks, Liverpool let potential victory slip away here in a concerning manner.

Trey Nyoni's first goal for the club had given them an early lead, but the teenager's deflected strike was cancelled out by Greenwood's reply in kind four minutes later.

The real drama came from the 69th minute to the 79th, with Liverpool inching ahead again, close to a fourth win in four in the competition, but unable to see the job through.

"It feels like a step back from what we saw against Arsenal because everyone thought, OK, we are seeing huge improvements from Liverpool," said ex-Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock, who was watching the game for Match of the Day.

"It was a much-changed team. However, the simple mistakes that they made from set-pieces or simple balls into the box are not good enough.

"The frustrating part for Liverpool fans is that we all know what the problems are. So, where is the solution? That's what Iraola is trying to find at the moment, but it's just a question of how long it takes.

"The biggest issue is that this keeps on happening, with Liverpool looking like they can concede at any moment and being so open on the counter-attack. There is a repetitive theme of the goals they are conceding and it undoes all the good work they do when they go forward.

"When you go ahead, twice, away from home at Fenerbahce in the Champions League then, if that is Arsenal they win that game - they see it out against a team like Fenerbahce.

"Liverpool don't have the ability to do that at the moment, and that is what is really frustrating."

Liverpool fan critical of Jeremy Jacquet performance

Dirk Kuyt was a passionate presence on the touchline for Fenerbahce

On the eve of this game in the Kadikoy neighbourhood of Istanbul, Kuyt spoke passionately about how Fenerbahce had the opportunity to show Europe their true colours.

He will step aside now, with former Newcastle player Emre Belozoglu taking over as head coach.

But thanks to this night, the continent saw what Fenerbahce can do.

They have had a torrid season so far, though, having lost four of their 10 league games and taken a 6-0 drubbing at Aston Villa, but Kuyt's men delivered a performance that will live long in the memory for anyone associated with the club.

"We showed Europe how big Fenerbahce is. This is what the spirit of this side is," said Kuyt.

"I think it's very special that for the first time since 18 years, Fenerbahce win a game against [an English side].

"Some people will remember but the number on the back of my shirt was 18 in Liverpool. So that's something really special for me.

"I said exactly the same thing to the players before the game. Although we are in a very difficult situation, we have a chance to bring another miracle in Istanbul. And if you get that miracle, things can change in a positive way."

They delivered in style, with 24-year-old former Derby County prospect Brown getting a goal and an assist in the second half.

"The Champions League is a great opportunity for Archie to show himself," said Kuyt.

"It's well known how good a player he is in Turkey. He did a fantastic job today. His defence and attack were very good. I'm very pleased with his performance, I'm pleased with the performance of all my players.

"It's a very special night for everyone who loves Fenerbahce."

#716. FA and WSL launch major study into ACL injuries in women's football

Leah Williamson, Beth Mead and Mary Fowler have all experienced ACL injuries

The Football Association and WSL Football have launched a major research project to better understand why anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injuries occur in women's football and identify ways to reduce them.

Funded by the FA, the PhD study with Imperial College London and sports knee surgeon Simon Ball will be led by researcher Hanna Lehtovirta and involve clubs across the Women's Super League and WSL2.

ACL injuries are among the most serious issues facing the women's game, often keeping players out for months.

Research suggests female footballers are two to six times more likely to suffer the injury than their male counterparts.

Vivianne Miedema, Beth Mead, Leah Williamson and Sam Kerr are among the players to have suffered the injury over recent years.

While previous studies have highlighted potential risk factors including anatomical, hormonal, biomechanical and environmental influences, researchers say less is known about how those factors interact in the day-to-day experience of elite football.

The study aims to provide one of the most comprehensive examinations of ACL injuries in women's football by combining scientific data with the experiences of players and staff.

Players from every WSL and WSL2 club will be invited to take part, alongside medical, performance and coaching staff.

The research will be conducted in two phases.

The first will use player surveys to gather data on injury history, training and match load, and hormonal, nutritional and psychological factors.

Data from players who have suffered ACL injuries since 2018-19 will be compared with those who have not.

The second phase will involve interviews with players and staff to explore perceptions of ACL injuries and current approaches to training and prevention.

Researchers hope the findings will help shape future injury prevention, rehabilitation and player welfare strategies in the women's game.

In April 2025, Fifa announced they were also funding research into whether hormonal fluctuations during menstrual cycles could be contributing to the rise in ACL injuries in women's football.

#715. Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson

There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long

Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsman as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome accept that that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye?

The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness that we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness that he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back.

At the 2022 World Cup, Fernando Santos belatedly took the decision to leave Ronaldo out for the last-16 tie against Switzerland. Portugal suddenly had a fluency and fluidity they had lacked for years and the player who had replaced Ronaldo, Gonçalo Ramos, scored a hat-trick . That seemed incontrovertible evidence that the end was upon Ronaldo, or at least that his role might become that of an impact substitute.

But even in the final minutes of that game, half the crowd were chanting for Ronaldo. Some, perhaps, were Portuguese fans but many were tourists. They didn’t care much about the result or who went through, they just wanted to see the famous man do the famous thing. Near the end, Ronaldo scored a goal that was obviously offside. He knew it was offside, but he also knew what his public wanted. So he did the “Siuuuu …” celebration and was rewarded with the biggest cheer of the night. This was like seeing late-period Elvis in Las Vegas: it didn’t matter he was no longer the singer he had been, he was still Elvis. It’s just that Elvis wasn’t also carrying Portugal’s World Cup hopes on his rhinestoned shoulders.

When a player has such celebrity status, when he is still somehow the show no matter how sluggish his movements, making that decision on when to quit must become even harder. And Ronaldo, with his status as Portugal’s greatest soft power export, also became a political issue. A cabinet minister publicly said he couldn’t be dropped because of how much revenue he generated and what he meant for Portugal’s brand. Portugal is not a country replete with global superstars.

Ronaldo hung around at Euro 2024, weeping after missing a penalty against Slovenia, the magnitude of his fame and ego warping perception so everything became about him, no matter how many other hugely gifted players were in that squad. And implausibly he was still doing it at the World Cup this summer: gumming the mechanisms, constantly demanding the ball, occasionally drifting out to the left to get in Rafael Leão’s way. At one point against Spain in what turns out to have been his final World Cup game, Ronaldo was released on the break but, lacking pace, ended up having to turn back and play the ball to his full-back, the opportunity gone. There was something almost painful about seeing a player once so explosive reduced to this.

There needed to be some sort of intervention. This generation of Portuguese players, who really should be challenging for major honours and not just the Nations League, could not continue to struggle on with such an albatross around their necks. It came from Jorge Jesus, the admirably forthright 72-year-old national coach, who was appointed after the World Cup. He didn’t bring Ronaldo off the bench in the second half of a tight game Portugal ended up winning against Norway. Ronaldo insisted he had been promised minutes – but even if there had been an agreement, it would be absurd to refuse a coach the capacity to adapt to circumstance – and stormed out of the camp, an indication perhaps of how his self-regard had come to distort his judgment.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

And, assuming this retirement isn’t some sort of powerplay to force Jesus out, that is where it ended, with a €255 fine and 30-day ban over a period in which Portugal had no games. Ronaldo will go back to the Saudi Pro League to continue his pursuit of a 1,000th goal.

He has been an extraordinary player. He will be remembered as an all-time great, vying with Eusébio as the greatest Portugal player of all time, but his legacy is undoubtedly tainted by this protracted farewell, by the sense that a player who at his best could win games single-handed, came by the end to be a burden to his national team. His has been a great career, but it would have been greater had it been a little shorter.

#714. Cardi B Reveals Name of Baby No. 4, Her First With Stefon Diggs

Cardi B announced the name of her and NFL player Stefon Diggs' baby boy, who she revealed last November that they had welcomed.

Cardi B revealed the name of her and NFL player Stefon Diggs' baby boy in honor of his first birthday. While Cardi shares kids Kulture, 8, Wave, 5, and Blossom, 2, with ex Offset, her youngest son is her first child with the New England Patriots wide receiver.

"Happy 1st birthday to Grey Marsean Diggs!!" Cardi wrote on Instagram Nov. 4 alongside sweet pictures of Grey. "It’s only been 1 year since meeting you but it feels like I’ve had you at my side forever. I carried you through one of the most uncertain high pressured times of my life but having you inside of me through it all gave me a extra strength."

That’s why her little guy’s name serves as a special reminder to keep her spirits up.

“I was growing you inside of me and at the same time you were giving me life!” she added. “You gave a new meaning to what a Grey day feels like. You light up my life and every room with your smile your laugh and your precious spirit.”

And, naturally, the mom of four made sure her son’s first Halloween had a sweet link to his moniker. After all, she also shared an adorable pic of the toddler sporting scrubs while sitting in front of a Grey’s Anatomy sign.

The "Hello" rapper’s post also marked the reveal of her baby's birth date. Last year, she shared that she welcomed her newest addition through a message marking her life changes in November.

"A new baby into my world, and one more reason to be the best version of me, one more reason to love me more than anything else or anyone else so I can continue giving my babies the love and life they deserve," she captioned her post at the time, a video of her strutting and striking poses to her song "Hello." She continued, "This next chapter is Me vs. Me!"

And the next chapter already looks good on her. Just hours after the announcement that she's now a mom of four, Cardi stepped out with Stefon for the launch party of baby brand Cybex’s flagship store in New York City, rocking a dramatic all-black ensemble featuring a corseted puffer coat, bubble skirt and fur detailing.

While Cardi opted to keep her lips sealed regarding her baby boy's name at the time, she did hint that it was one she really loved.

"I'm not sharing the name yet," she told Highsnobiety at the Cybex event. "It's cute."

While the name stayed under wraps, the 34-year-old did share a bit into what her birth and post-partum experience has been like, adding, "You know, I was a little bit on bed rest because that baby, oh, that baby was heavy."

However, her toughness is what she hopes her children will learn from her.

"I will stand up for myself," she said of how she leads by example. "Sometimes people be like, 'Oh no avoid it.' No, I will stand up for myself. Then my kids can see that they mama ain't no punk."

For more Cardi B moments that will make your say "Okurrr," read on.

"She broke my vagina," Cardi B told Jimmy Kimmel while recalling the birth of her daughter, Kulture Kiari. "Nobody told me they were gonna stitch my vagina."

"Shoes? $1,200. These glasses? $400. But bitch, my outfit? $20 dollars bitch," she exclaimed in a since-deleted Instagram post. "Get yourself together bitch. Learn how to budget hoe."

"NOTHING LAST FOREVER EXCEPT BILLS," she declared on Twitter when a fan asked for help choosing a senior quote. To be fair, she's not wrong.

"My boyfriend at the time—he dumped me two weeks before my prom, but I honestly think it was because he didn't want to pay for the limo, but then that night…forget it," she told Jimmy Fallon and John Mulaney on The Tonight Show. "The limo that I ended up with—I didn't rented it…I just got in a limo and just…forget it. I can't get into it. Kids watch me now."

"Once you start making money, everybody wants you to be their kid's godmother," she quipped on The Tonight Show.

"I want to thank my fans—Bardi Gang—because even when I'm wrong they be like, 'She still right' and I want to thank my haters, too, because they be downloading my stuff so they can hear it and talk crap about it, but it benefits me!" she said while accepting the Best New Artist Award at the 2018 iHeartRadio Music Awards.

"I'm just a regular, degular, shmegular girl from the Bronx," the former reality star has said often on Love & Hip Hop.

"If he has sex with you more than five times, he loves you," she told BET in 2017.

#711. Germany takes cautious approach on Israeli election results

German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

Though it has been two days since Israel's parliamentary elections, German politicians are still being cautious to respond, as it is still unclear who will lead Israel's new government.

Although the right-wing bloc, including religious hardliners, led by incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is ahead of the opposition bloc led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, neither has a clear path to a governing majority in the Knesset.

Forming a coalition government is likely to be extremely difficult.

Martin Giese, spokesperson for German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, declined to comment at Wednesday's regular government press conference in Berlin.

But he did stress that Germany has been in contact with numerous officials and politicians in Israel via Germany's ambassador. "The Jewish state and Germany are inextricably linked by our history, and we will do everything we can to work well with any future government," Wadephul said.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

One concern for the German government is providing aid to the people in Gaza, and protracted coalition negotiations could delay necessary progress.

"Winter is coming, and it will be difficult," Development Minister Reem Alabali Radovan, currently visiting Lebanon, warned in an interview with Politico. She underlined that there must be more opportunities for aid organizations to provide crucial assistance in Gaza and that it cannot wait for coalition negotiations.

In interviews with DW and broadcaster RTL, she spoke about the recent increase in attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and East Jerusalem.

"The radical settler violence must be stopped. The Netanyahu government remains in office on an interim basis, and this means that this situation must still be brought to an end," she said.

All settlement activity in the occupied Palestinian territories is considered illegal under international law.

Relations between Germany and Israel are traditionally close, in part because of Germany's historical responsibility for Nazi Germany's murder of millions of Jews during the Holocaust.

Recently, however, the German government has distanced itself from Netanyahu's policies, at least in its public rhetoric.

Most recently, Wadephul said after a major Israeli military operation near the city of Hebron: "Under international law, Israel is quite clearly obligated to uphold and protect the rights of Palestinians as well." Around 3,000 Palestinians were driven from their homes during the operation, which followed the reported killing of two Israeli soldiers by Palestinians.

In Berlin, there has long been speculation about whether Germany's policy toward Israel might change after Israel's 2026 election.

So far, one thing is clear: Unlike numerous other countries, including some in Europe, Germany does not intend to recognize a Palestinian state for the time being.

At the same time, Germany hopes that the future government will no longer include religious extremists, and in some cases far-right, politicians such as the current Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich.

"I think it would be best for Israel to form a government that is closer to the center of the political spectrum," Jürgen Hardt, foreign policy expert for the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) in the Bundestag, told DW. "Of course, that's something the people, and above all the elected politicians, will have to figure out. But it's encouraging that so many people participated in the election."

The Arab-majority parties led by Palestinian citizens of Israel made large gains in this election. They are usually classified as part of the current opposition camp. The historic results by these parties could lead them to play a kingmaker role in coalition formation.

However, Netanyahu’s bloc have ruled out working with the Arab-majority parties.

Eisenkot's opposition bloc has not yet said whether it would be willing to form such a coalition, but one of the Arab-majority parties, United Arab List/Ra'am, featured a Jewish candidate, and has stated its willingness to work with Eisenkot’s bloc to unseat Netanyahu.

Hardt believes a minority government led by Eisenkot and supported by parties representing Arab Israelis is conceivable.

"The major campaign carried out by Netanyahu's camp, aimed primarily against Arab Israelis, greatly mobilized the opposition, to the point where his camp no longer has a majority."

The vice president of the German Bundestag, Green Party politician Omid Nouripour, told DW: "Frankly, after all the turmoil that has occurred — for example, regarding judicial reform — this is good news for Israeli democracy."

This article was originally published in German.

Liftoff of the NVS-03 mission occurred at 2:21 p.m. ET today (Oct. 30).

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

India bolstered its homegrown satellite-navigation system today (Oct. 30).

A GSLV Mark II rocket launched the nation's NVS-03 satellite from Satish Dhawan Space Centre today at 2:21 p.m. EDT (1821 GMT and 11:51 p.m. India Standard Time).

Everything went well: The rocket deployed NVS-03 into geostationary transfer orbit as planned, officials with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) announced on X about 30 minutes after liftoff.

NVS-03 is the third next-gen satellite that India has launched for the Navigation with Indian Constellation (NavIC), its version of the United States' Global Positioning System (GPS).

NavIC operates on a smaller scale than its American counterpart, however. It's "a regional navigation satellite system designed to provide accurate Position, Navigation and Timing (PNT) service to users in India as well as the region extending about 1,500 km [930 miles] beyond the Indian landmass, which is its primary service area," ISRO officials wrote in the NVS-03 launch brochure.

The Indian constellation currently consists of three fully functioning satellites, and it requires four to provide PNT services. So today's launch was a big deal — and a lot of eyes will be watching NVS-03's commissioning and checkout phase.

Today's launch was the 14th to date for the GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) Mark II, a three-stage rocket that stands 170 feet (52 meters) tall. Twelve of those 14 liftoffs have been successful.

The GSLV Mark II debuted in 2010, the same year its predecessor retired. That previous launchers, the Mark I, flew a total of six times, with two failures.

NVS-03 was the fourth Indian launch of 2026 and the third operated by ISRO. The fourth was mounted by Skyroot Aerospace, which in July became the first Indian company ever to successfully reach orbit.

Tara Lipinski is surprised how her daughter is skating to her own tune.

Set against a changing America, The Greatest follows a once-in-a-generation talent fighting for the right to become his own man. Through the fights that made him a champion and the convictions that made him an icon, a young man from Louisville transforms himself into Muhammad Ali, the greatest of all time.

Taken: Natalee Holloway (Netflix) - Nov. 4

On May 30, 2005, 18-year-old Natalee Holloway vanished on a high school graduation trip to Aruba—and never came home. What followed was years of unanswered questions, a missing teenager, and a mother's relentless fight for the truth. Now, over 20 years later, Natalee's mother, Beth, is ready to tell the complete story. With exclusive, unprecedented access to Beth and those who were with Natalee when she vanished, this three-part documentary series is the definitive account of a case that gripped a nation and never let go. It's a story of a mother who refused to stop searching, an investigation that spanned continents, and a daughter whose memory endures. This is Natalee's story, told at last in full.

Helen (Keira Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organization she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever.

Awkwafina: The Unlikely Cook (Apple TV) - Nov. 6

The eight-episode series follows Nora Lum, aka Awkwafina, on a cross-country culinary road trip as she attempts to revive her family’s beloved Chinese restaurant.

Wolves Up Close With Bertie Gregory (National Geographic) - Nov. 6

Reconnecting with a pack of wolves he has followed for seven years, Bertie Gregory sets out to capture one of the Arctic’s most dangerous and rarely filmed hunts: wolves taking on a bull moose, prey roughly ten times their size. Led by Kona, a striking white breeding male, the pack faces a critical winter as dwindling food supplies, an encroaching rival wolf and an aging leader threaten its survival.

Charmed By a Southern Monster (Peacock) - Nov. 9

Starring Craig Conover as Hunter Caldwell and Nicole Mattox as Maeve Marchant, the series blends soapy romance, workplace rivalry and small-town mystery.

The story follows Maeve, a brilliant corporate fixer sent to convince and seduce Hunter, a rumored murderer, into selling his family’s estate. But when she discovers that the town’s most feared man may actually be its most misunderstood, and the only person who can protect her from her dangerous ex-boyfriend, Maeve becomes entangled in Hunter’s world. As family secrets and a billion-dollar development deal threaten to unravel their growing connection, she must confront her past and decide how much she’s willing to risk for love.

Whitney Way Thore is stepping into a transformative new chapter. Back in her home state of North Carolina, Whitney has found love with Jake, a man she first met years ago before reconnecting after her return to Charlotte. As their relationship deepens, Whitney is rediscovering her confidence through dance, exploring new possibilities on her health journey, and taking meaningful steps toward the future she’s always wanted, including her biggest dream of becoming a mom.

Picking up after the gut-wrenching mid-series finale, Tony Baddingham and Declan O'Hara's battle for the Cotswolds crown reaches fever pitch, while Rupert Campbell-Black is forced to confront his own personal demons. Against a backdrop of hedonistic parties, Bonfire Night chaos, the Hampshire Hunt Ball and a turbulent Christmas, affairs unravel, alliances fracture and rivalries intensify. Caught in the middle of the frenzied franchise war, Taggie O'Hara must find the courage to follow her heart, while those around her face the consequences of ambition, power and secrets that can no longer remain hidden. But as series two draws to a close, who will get their happy ending?

From Ron Howard, the documentary explores the life, career, and cultural impact of legendary American photographer Richard Avedon.

The Good Daughter is a suspenseful thriller wrapped in a deeply emotional story about love, family and resilience. Sisters Charlotte (Meghann Fahy) and Samantha (Rose Byrne) Quinn have spent the last 20 years trying to piece together the lives that were fractured by a single night of violence. When another attack splinters the small town of Pikeville, Charlotte – now a lawyer like her father – is the first witness on the scene. As the case unfolds and twists through painful memories and buried secrets, what emerges is not just a story of survival, but of enduring ties between a father and his daughters, and the complex bond between sisters.

After a reunion where the status of friendships and situationships remained ambiguous, the Charmers are determined to define their relationships and mend wounds. However, when true feelings bubble up and juicy rumors catch fire, the group seeks to unveil the truth – even if it costs them more than just friendships.

Three years into their jobs as response officers, Constables Grace Ellis, Tommy Foster, and Annie Conlon are operating at their limit, facing a new threat on the streets that the police can barely control. Meanwhile the murder trial of Gerry Cliff exposes a dangerous and long-buried secret that leads to chaos both inside the police, and across the criminal underworld. As they grapple with big decisions about their future, Grace, Tommy and Annie must find the courage to face the greatest threat they have ever encountered: the truth.

Each episode of the drama unfolds across three timelines of a heist: the 12 months of planning, the 12 hours of the heist, and the 12 days following the heist. The series follows a disgraced FBI agent (Anthony Mackie) and an American career criminal (Jamie Dornan) who play a zero-sum game of cat and mouse across Europe. At the center of it all is the daring, epic raid on a bank vault deep beneath the streets of Zurich.

Expedition: Saving Our Seas (National Geographic) - Nov. 13

The documentary follows teams of National Geographic Explorers as they investigate our global Ocean, from seashore to seafloor and pole to pole. Combining cutting-edge technology with the knowledge of coastal communities, they chase the discoveries and solutions needed to protect our Oceans at a critical moment.

Homicide for the Holidays (Oxygen) - Nov. 14

The holidays are supposed to be the most wonderful time of the year. But for some families, cherished celebrations become the backdrop for unimaginable violence. Season six of Homicide For The Holidays brings a new batch of deadly deeds to the supposed jolliest time of the year as investigators pursue those responsible and seek justice for families shattered at a time meant for togetherness.

Diane Morgan returns as Philomena Cunk in a new series from Charlie Brooker. Billed as Cunk's most glamorous outing yet, she charts the history of cinema, from the invention of the camera and the New Wave filmmakers of the 1960s right up to the entrance of CGI and what the future of AI holds. Cunk will attempt to demystify it all while sitting in lumpy seats with stale popcorn, asking herself where did cinema come from? And why? What does it want? And why can’t it tell us?

Small Town Trouble: Texas (Bravo) - Nov. 18

Set in Boerne (pronounced "Bur-nee"), Texas, the series follows a charming yet unconventional group of wives, mothers and social insiders – Aaryn Williams, Alli McAnelly, Annari Uys, Gabby Hernandez Huffman, and Hailey Head, alongside their respective husbands – as conservative values of small-town life collide with forbidden attraction, messy friendships, and shocking   secrets. Here, perception is everything, temptation is everywhere, and the truth is never as buttoned-up as it looks.

The story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye - before they were accused of stealing $8 billion and became Gen Z's own Bonnie & Clyde.

Nelly and Ashanti: We Belong Together (Peacock) - Nov. 19

This season, Ashanti continues to balance motherhood, continuing to perform on stage, and taking control of her musical legacy. While navigating living in St. Louis and New York City, Ashanti also juggles re-recording her debut album to retain her masters, finding time for her girlfriends who keep her grounded, and recording new music with some of music's hottest artists. After years of nonstop touring, Nelly reflects on the physical toll it’s taking at this stage in his life, and an unexpected family loss reminds him what matters most. Between raising their son, honoring their village, and planning for their future, Nelly and Ashanti discover that belonging together isn’t about standing still; it’s about building a future on their own terms.

Nearly a decade after a mysterious female jogger dubbed “The Mad Pooper” captured national attention for repeatedly defecating on residential lawns across Colorado Springs, one of the strangest unsolved mysteries is back in the spotlight. In the new two-hour special, viewers will dive headfirst into the bizarre true story that left an entire community searching for answers and asking one simple question: why?

As the survivors race to bury their sins before rescue arrives and an old flame roars back into town with plans of her own, turns out not every homecoming is a joyous one, and this one's going to sting.

Adapted from Tom Bradby's bestselling novel, Secret Service follows senior MI6 officer Kate Henderson (Gemma Arterton), whose covert investigation uncovers evidence that a high-ranking U.K. politician may be working as a Russian asset. With trust shattered and her career on the line, Kate must navigate the shifting sands of political loyalty, international threat, and personal sacrifice as she races to uncover their identity before it's too late.

The new comedy follows a team of dedicated archaeologists (and less-dedicated college students) who spend their summer working on a dig site in Greece. Their discovery of a rare artifact sends them on the adventure of a lifetime.

Living under pressure can significantly impact the cognitive abilities of aquanauts — people living underwater for more than a day.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Our time on our "space mission" underwater was coming to an end, and I felt like what I imagine an astronaut on the International Space Station (ISS) must feel before returning to Earth. On one hand, you are excited to return to your home and loved ones, as well as to fresh food and normal hygiene. On the other, you know you will miss your crew and the incredible experience of being in space.

While my SEA STAR crew and I had not left Earth during our mission, we were separated from the surface of our home planet for five days. All we saw was a green alien water world surrounding us. We did this to live and work like astronauts on the ISS. Instead of dealing with the challenges of space that astronauts face, we problem-solved sometimes equally difficult issues that divers have to manage when performing research in sea water.

Our "wet ISS" was the Jules' Undersea Lab, which is located near Key Largo, Florida, at 22 feet (7 meters) underwater. By the end of our mission, we had all officially become aquanauts. An aquanaut is an undersea explorer who remains underwater for more than 24 hours, without returning to the surface, in a state known as saturation.

In this sense, saturation refers to the physiological condition achieved by a person who breathes underwater long enough for the body's tissues to absorb the maximum possible amount of inert gas (like nitrogen), for a specific depth and pressure. The term aquanaut derives from the Latin word "aqua" (water) and the Greek "nautes" (sailor).

There were a lot of things I wasn't going to miss about being an aquanaut. They included the constant loud noises our life support systems made to keep us alive underwater, as well as bathroom plumbing issues and some health concerns linked to living under pressure. We also had to be very careful when performing our "spacewalks" (scuba dives), due to the low visibility of the environment around us.

Nonetheless, I experienced a sort of "underview effect" during this mission. Most astronauts report experiencing an "overview effect" after seeing our whole planet from space, which usually makes them value our unique planet even more. I felt a similar thing when I saw the sun's rays come through the water. I couldn't reach them, but I enjoyed them from afar. My everyday life felt so close, yet so far away. It gave me both a feeling of longing and more determination to take even more care of our home world than before.

I'm grateful that we were able to perform all of the different scientific projects we planned for our mission. As the Commander of the crew, I usually have my work cut out for me managing the crew and overseeing their research projects, as had been the case for most of the 40 simulated space missions that I led previously. Fortunately, this time my crew was made up of experienced analog astronauts and divers, so the mission was mostly smooth sailing.

The research we chose for this mission was relevant for long-duration space missions. Since we can only send a small number of astronauts to the ISS with a limited number of research activities to perform, underwater stations provide us with a valuable way to conduct analog, or simulated, space missions instead. We also performed some environmental conservation work using a type of underwater vacuum device to help protect the nature around the Jules' Undersea Lab.

My scientific project was focused on studying whether our cognitive abilities and reaction times changed under pressure. This study is part of my collaboration with the Center for Hyperbaric Medicine, Faculty of Medicine of the University of Ostrava and City Hospital Ostrava in the Czech Republic. The whole crew definitely felt like their response times to these tests were slower during the mission than before it.

We were also interested in seeing how microgreens seeds were affected by the changes in pressure. Our Health & Safety Officer, Dr. Brandy Nunez, grew some of our kale and super salad mix before we started our mission, while other seeds started their growth journey underwater. All seeds were transferred to our underwater station using two varied pressure settings (gradual and sudden pressure release during their descent). After we harvested them, we could see that the latter types of seeds did indeed experience some barotrauma (damage caused by the sudden increase in air pressure).

Executive Officer Paul Bakken's work was related to managing the internal pressure of logistical transfer containers when they are exposed to significant environmental changes in pressure. The fourth crewmember, Mission Specialist Jenn Pint, worked with Interstellar Performance Labs to develop a taxonomy for analyzing environmental and crew interaction factors during simulated space missions.

On top of these projects, we also performed neutral buoyancy experiments during our underwater spacewalks, as well as the testing of environmental sensors developed by high school and university students in Slovakia. The sensors provided important supplemental information to the cognitive study about our simulated space habitat's living conditions.

Just like astronauts on the ISS, we dedicated some of our time to outreach and educational work, too. In our case, we called Cosmic Region, a simulated space station in Slovakia, and gave the team there a tour of our underwater habitat. My crewmembers kindly went into the water at that time and performed a spacewalk to show what our work during the mission was like.

As I put on my "spacesuit" (scuba diving gear) one last time, I breathed the stuffy undersea air once more and then dove out to return to "Earth." My crewmembers and I then took a long detour around the lagoon around us to help our bodies adjust to lower pressures. Even though we were only 22 feet underwater, there was still a small risk of decompression-related problems that aquanauts can face after living under saturation for some time. The final step was to breach the surface at long last. That's when we all enjoyed breathing fresh air again and feeling the sun on our faces, though the temperature in Florida made us quickly hide away from it again 😉.

You can follow Dr. Michaela Musilova at her website and on social media: @astro_michaela (Instagram, TikTok and Threads), @Dr. Michaela Musilova (Facebook) and @astro-michaela.bsky.social (Bluesky).

Dr. Michaela Musilova is an award-winning astrobiologist, explorer, professional speaker and author. Michaela has been conducting space-related research at institutions around the world, including NASA, ESA, CalTech, the Canada-France-Hawaii telescope and many others. She was the Commander of 40 simulated missions to the Moon and Mars — the most missions led to date.

"He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love."

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess.

We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four "Star Trek" feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more.

"Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love."

William Shatner, a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations."

"What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed."

Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s "Star Trek: Picard" and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death

"Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more."

Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession.

"There's no one on this planet that I have acted with or directed more often than my late great friend Patrick Stewart," revealed actor and director Jonathan Frakes, who co-starred for over 35 years with Stewart as Commander Will Riker, in a touching statement. "He will be with me forever. May he rest in Peace."

Finally, Marina Sirtis posted a teary-eyed video in which she explained how much of an impact Stewart had on her life during their time together on "The Next Generation" series and films, in which she portrayed Counselor Deanna Troi beside him.

"Patrick, I loved you with all my heart," she said on Instagram. "I know you're up there now, reunited with all those that you've loved. But to say that you'll be missed down here is probably the understatement of the century. It was an honor to work with Patrick. It was more than an honor; it was the privilege of my life to work with him."

Jeff Spry is an award-winning screenwriter and veteran freelance journalist covering TV, movies, video games, books, and comics. His work has appeared at SYFY Wire, Inverse, Collider, Bleeding Cool and elsewhere. Jeff lives in beautiful Bend, Oregon amid the ponderosa pines, classic muscle cars, a crypt of collector horror comics, and two loyal English Setters.

#706. Why Matthew Stafford’s Wife Kelly Stafford Is Calling Out the NFL

Kelly Stafford, wife of Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, questioned the NFL's decision to schedule the Los Angeles team's bye week with only 10 days off, rather than the usual 11 to 14.

Kelly Stafford is throwing a flag on the NFL's schedule.

As the Los Angeles Rams continue to hit the field during the 2026 season, quarterback Matthew Stafford's wife sent a pointed message to the league about the team's calendar.

"Just curious to hear the thought process behind making the Rams the only team in the NFL without a true bye week," Kelly wrote on her Instagram Stories Nov. 3. "Because damn, after 18 years around this league, even I need a week off during the season… and I have never played a single snap."

The registered nurse—who shares 9-year-old twin girls Sawyer and Chandler, as well as daughters Hunter, 8, and Tyler, 6, with Matthew—may not be lacing up her cleats, but she knows when a time-out may be needed.

"I'm tired just watching from the stands," she continued. "Can't imagine how the guys feel."

Although teams generally have their bye weeks after a Sunday game and don't play again for 11 to 14 days, both the Rams and Green Bay Packers—who face off on the day before Thanksgiving (Nov. 25)—will return to the field after 10 days.

Other teams with a bye week at the same time, including the Cleveland Browns, New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, will still take a full 14 days off.

E! News has reached out to the NFL for comment and has not yet heard back.

Not every schedule may be a touchdown, but the league does try its best to ensure each team has a restful week off, which is determined by the number of cross-country games scheduled, stadium conflicts and other operational obstacles.

"The scheduling teams aim to balance these operational elements while still trying to maximize fan viewership," the NFL Operations website explained. "The process is challenging, and there may be no such thing as a perfect schedule, but the schedule makers consistently try to provide the NFL's fans and broadcast partners with a compelling and entertaining slate of games week after week."

While Kelly is willing to call a foul on the Rams' calendar, she will always cheer on her husband, who has been her MVP since they married in 2015.

"He is the softest, most patient man," she told E! News in 2022. "My dad always said one of the most important relationships in life is a father-daughter relationship just because of the confidence your dad can give you."

"I am so grateful that I ended up with Matthew," she added, "because he sets such an incredible example as to the partner they should want to be with."

As the Staffords prepare for another week of football, keep reading for a closer look at their game-winning family moments.

On the field, Matthew Stafford is one of the best quarterbacks of the NFL. But when the football player comes home, he's simply dad.

During bye-week, Matthew and his wife Kelly Stafford treated their kids to a festive fall day near their home in Los Angeles.

"33 and grateful for the people that fill this home," Kelly wrote when celebrating her birthday. "Thankful for these girls' contagious smiles and for a husband who never fails to make me laugh."

"A pier breakfast, turned beach day, turned watching pro female surfing competition…" Kelly wrote on Instagram. "Pretty epic summer day with great 'aloha vibes.'"

After playing at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles, Matthew was able to reunite with three of his daughters in a suite.

After cheering for Dad all day long, it's no surprise that Matthew's kids just want to snuggle after game day.

Whether they are at the stadium or going to school, Matthew's daughters love to wear the Rams' team colors.

When Matthew worked from home during COVID-19 shutdowns, his daughters quickly wore him out.

"My whole heart in one photo," Kelly wrote on Instagram when capturing her daughters snuggling by Matthew.

#705. Japan's Tashima to stand against Infantino for Fifa presidency

Kozo Tashima became president of the Japan Football Association in 2016

The Japan Football Association honorary president, Kozo Tashima, has announced his intention to stand against Gianni Infantino to be the next Fifa president.

Tashima, 68, is a member of the Fifa Council and a former international footballer and coach.

He said he wants to convey "integrity, soundness, and high moral standards" and "contribute to a better future for football".

Infantino has been under intense scrutiny since it emerged he had been planning to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

The Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was abandoned at the end of July, after significant backlash from across world football.

The deadline for candidates to stand in the election is 18 November.

Whilst support for Infantino was severely impacted by the FFE scandal, he has shored up support in recent months.

Infantino told BBC Sport last month that he felt he had the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football as he bids for a fourth term in charge of Fifa.

His comments came after he was "fully endorsed" by the Asian Football Confederation - following a U-turn by its president Sheikh Salman.

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put their name forward in October for next year's Fifa presidential election.

However, Tashima's emergence as a challenger - with the backing of the Japan Football Association (JFA) - will now test the strength of Infantino's supporter base.

As with all candidates, Tashima will require the backing of five Fifa member associations.

Infantino laughs off resignation questions

Announcing his intentions, Tashima said: "I believe it is important to clearly communicate to the world of football the integrity, soundness, and high moral standards that Japanese football has cherished and built up over the years.

"I have decided to run for Fifa presidential election in order to convey this philosophy to the world and contribute to a better future for football.

"I will take on this challenge with strong determination, making use of the experience I have cultivated so far, and contributing to the further development of world football."

Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, president of the JFA, said: "This decision is a major challenge to contribute to the further development of world football by utilising that experience and knowledge, and at the same time, we believe it will be an opportunity to show the world the ideals and attitudes that Japanese football has cherished."

#704. Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Nature (2026) Cite this article

We’re sharing this article early to provide faster access to peer-reviewed, accepted research. It is citable and carries a permanent DOI. This version is subject to further edits and will be replaced automatically by the final Version of Record. All legal disclaimers apply.

Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

It was the 118th Falcon 9 launch of the year so far.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

SpaceX celebrated Halloween with an early-morning launch from California.

A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today (Oct. 31) at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT; 9:04 p.m. on Oct. 30 local time), sending 27 of the company's Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO).

The Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth as planned, touching down about 8.5 minutes after launch on the SpaceX drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed in the Pacific Ocean.

It was the 18th flight for this particular booster, which is designated B1093. The record for a SpaceX first stage is 37, set this past August by the booster B1067.

The Falcon 9's upper stage did its job as well today, deploying the 27 Starlink satellites into LEO about 62 minutes after launch. They're joining more than 11,000 spacecraft in the Starlink megaconstellation, which is by far the largest satellite network ever assembled.

SDA-T1TL-B | SDA-T1TL-C | Transporter-16 | 14 Starlink missions

Today's launch was the 118th Falcon 9 flight of 2026 so far. More than 70% of these missions have been devoted to building out the Starlink network.

SpaceX has also launched its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times apiece this year. Falcon Heavy is an operational vehicle, but Starship remains in the test-flight phase. The company is currently gearing up for another Starship launch, which is expected to take place sometime in November.

Michael Wall is the Spaceflight and Tech Editor for Space.com and joined the team in 2010. He has a Ph.D. in evolutionary biology from the University of Sydney, Australia, a bachelor's degree from the University of Arizona, and a graduate certificate in science writing from the University of California, Santa Cruz.
